purpose: verified-pilot-3.3 MFPI: species-level aquaculture records read in the original source (workflow wf_65a66cfe-ab4: research, then an independent verifier re-opened every page; HTTP 200 without login, quotation found verbatim). One primary record per species.
rule: feasible = grow-out of this species documented from seed or juvenile to harvest, or through a full culture season, in a named system, region and period. A record whose trials stopped before grow-out is kept with feasible = false. Production counts alone are not proof. Flounder, croaker and blue crab were not confirmed in this search and are left to the separate team PR.

food_support.record_id: Report No. BSPM55350-2205-3 (제출문 dated 2010. 10). The quote is from the 요약문 (PDF p.vi region). Also cited: the section on larval rearing from Geoje eggs in a 12 m³ PP tank at 강원도립대학, followed to 33 days post-hatch; the conditioning section (4 m PP circular tanks (10 t), deep ocean water at 5-6 °C); and PDF p.x (offshore cage and economics).
food_support.method: Experimental land-based flow-through tank rearing of wild-caught Pacific cod juveniles from set nets. The fish were weaned on frozen krill, then moved to formulated/moist feeds, in 4 m PP circular tanks (10 t) and 2 m³ tanks supplied with deep ocean water held at 5-6 °C. Larvae were also reared in a 12 m³ PP tank to 33 days post-hatch from eggs stripped from wild broodstock landed at Geoje. The planned offshore submerged-cage grow-out was never stocked with cod.
food_support.region: Republic of Korea, East Sea coast: Goseong-gun, Gangwon-do (KORDI Deep Ocean Water Research Center), with juveniles from set nets off Ohori. Eggs came from Geoje (Gyeongsangnam-do), and larval rearing was done at the Gangwon Provincial College fish-culture facility.
food_support.limitations: Recorded as not feasible: the only Korean record is a 2007-2010 pilot that reared wild-caught juveniles in land tanks; no fish reached market size, the planned offshore-cage grow-out was never stocked, and the economic analysis found NPV < 0. This was a pilot/experimental study with capture-based seed. The January batch grew from about 57 g to 154 g in 130 days with 46% survival. The March batch lost biomass. No fish reached market size. The offshore cage (installed at 24 m depth) was trial-stocked with yellowtail (방어) in October 2009; that stock died off in January 2010 from a sudden temperature drop and the cage panels were damaged, so the cod stocking planned for May 2010 was cancelled. The economic analysis of offshore-cage cod culture found NPV < 0 and B/C < 1 in the scenarios. There is no evidence of commercial production.
food_support.quote: 자연산 대구를 인공적인 환경에서 안정적인 사육기술개발을 위해 연중 10℃이하로 유지가 가능한 해양심층수를 이용하여 자연의 주 먹이인 크릴새우를 대상으로 육상 수조에서 먹이붙임 실험을 실시하였고

food_support.record_id: The Introduction gives the Wando aquaculture history and production. The Abstract and Methods describe suspended cages in a 'submerged culture facility' off Wando Island (34°18′N), with sampling in May, August and November 2017 and February 2018.
food_support.method: Sea-based suspended (hanging) net-cage grow-out of H. discus hannai in a submerged culture facility
food_support.region: Wando Island, off the southwestern coast of the Korean Peninsula
food_support.year: Culture expanding since 1970; 12,000 t in 2016; field sampling 2017-2018; published 2019
food_support.limitations: This is a physiology study, not a culture-method paper. The method (suspended cage nets) and history are given as context. The production figure cites the MOF statistics portal. Subspecies hannai is an accepted subspecies of H. discus in WoRMS (re-checked 2026-09-30).
food_support.quote: Abalone aquaculture in the shallow coastal seas around Wando Island ... has been expanding since 1970, and the annual production reached 12,000 tonnes in 2016 ... abalone cultivated in suspended cage nets are exposed

food_support.record_id: Vol. 19, Issue 4, pp. 375-379 (published 1986-07-01). Korean abstract, opening sentence. The English abstract says seed shells 'were planted on bottom mud with a density 20 to 40 shells per square meter on March 10 and 11, 1982'.
food_support.method: Bottom culture (바닥식 양성): seed shells (mean 2.5 cm, 2.5 g) planted on bottom mud at 20-40 per m² in March 1982 and grown out to harvest in December 1983
food_support.region: Yoja Bay (여자만), western part of the south coast of Korea (남해 서부해역)
food_support.year: 1986 publication; culture from March 1982 to harvest in December 1983
food_support.limitations: This is a single-site field culture experiment. Growth was favourable (6.1 cm and 63.0 g after one year), but final survival was only about 10% at harvest, mainly because of starfish (Asterias spp.) predation. It shows technical feasibility with a large mortality constraint. The page does not say where the seed came from, so the earlier 'hatchery-size' wording was removed.
food_support.quote: 남해 서부해역에 위치한 여자만에서 바닥식으로 양성한 피조개, Anadara broughtonii에 관한 성장과 폐사에 관해 1982년 8월부터 6개월간 조사한 결과는 다음과 같다.

food_support.record_id: Final report TRKO201800002340, project no. 1525005011, DOI 10.23000/TRKO201800002340. The quote is in the Korean 초록 (cited as '출처 : 보고서 요약서 3p'). The table list includes '로프수하식 양성 시설 전경', '참담치 로프수하식 양성 전경', '로프수하식 양성시 수심에 따른 성장과 생존율' and '로프수하식 양성시 사육기간에 따른 생존율 변화'. The previously cited table name '로프수하식 로프 간양성장에서 참담치의 월별 생존율' does not appear on the page.
food_support.method: Rope hanging (suspended) grow-out culture (로프수하식). It outperformed basket hanging culture (채롱수하식). Raft-type intermediate nursery (the page writes '멧목식', a typo for 뗏목식) cut the nursery period by about 50% compared with 채롱수하식. Hatchery seed production used freshwater spawning stimulation. Horizontal-net culture (수평망식) on west-coast tidal flats was judged unsuitable.
food_support.region: South coast of Korea (남해안) for rope hanging grow-out. Grow-out sites in the table list are Geomundo and Dolsan-do, Yeosu (여수 거문도 / 돌산도 양성해역). The unsuccessful horizontal-net trial was on the west coast (Gunsan).
food_support.limitations: This is an R&D pilot and demonstration project, not proof of commercial-scale farming. The report says industrialisation would be effective 'if suitable sea areas are selected'. Only the ScienceON record page (Korean and English summaries plus table list) was verified. The full-text PDF was not opened.
food_support.quote: 남해안에서는 로프수하식 양성이 채롱수하식 양성보다 참담치 양성에 효율적인 것으로 나타났으며 참담치 양성에 적합한 해역이 선정된다면 산업화에 매우 효과적인 것으로 나타났다.

food_support.record_id: Abstract. Methods section II.2 (육상호지 양식장: Taean, Chungcheongnam-do, 500 tons, 17 × 30 m, depth 1 m). Results: at the end of the trial on 16 Nov, 440 individuals remained.
food_support.method: Land-based outdoor open tank/pond (육상호지) grow-out managed as flow-through (유수식), with no heating after early-season plastic covering. Broodstock were spawned in indoor tanks at the East Sea Fisheries Research Institute. About 50,000 attached eggs were stocked in May 2021: the English abstract says early May and the Korean Methods say mid-May (5월 중순). Hatchlings were fed live opossum shrimps (mysids), and frozen shrimp were fed from August.
food_support.region: Taean, Chungcheongnam-do, Korea (broodstock from Sacheon port, South Sea)
food_support.year: Trial April-November 2021; accepted 1 Dec 2023; published December 2023
food_support.limitations: This is a single experimental trial and the first Korean report. Survival was low (440 of about 50,000 eggs at the end), and growth varied widely between individuals. The authors frame it as an 'aquaculture possibility', not commercial practice. The species is listed as Sepia esculenta, a superseded combination of Acanthosepion esculentum in WoRMS (re-checked 2026-09-30).
food_support.quote: Approximately 50,000 eggs were transferred to the open tank in early May ... the confirmation of fast-growing cuttlefish suggests the aquaculture possibility of cuttlefish in the open tank
